title: Lace Anatomy: Tx Viewer and Builder by TxPipe

ms.promise: Implementation of an MVP for a webapp that is able to draw a transaction from a CBOR or a tx hash making the necessary queries to some blockchain indexer.
ms.criteria: The webapp can read a CBOR or a tx hash and display the diagram of a transaction with arrows for inputs and outputs, showing in a user-friendly way the main information: utxos’ value and datums, minted and burned tokens, tx fees, among others.
ms.report:
Milestone goals and proofs of completion

A web app that can draw a transaction from a CBOR or a tx hash. 

We implemented a web app that can read a CBOR or a Transaction Hash and display the diagram of a transaction represented with a box with lines for inputs and outputs. The source code is publicly available in the following repository:
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx
Milestone 1 was divided into two main stages:
The first stage focuses on functionality developed from a CBOR:
・First, we added and refactored the initial prototype that was presented during the proposal submission phase.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/1
・Next, we added a panel to display transaction related information, such as the hash, fee, minting/burning details, among other data.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/2 https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/3
・Then, we included information about reference inputs.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/4 
・We also added a feature to name transactions (or assign an alias).

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/5 
・Finally, we added a panel to display information about UTxOs. Previously, only the UTxO reference for inputs was shown. 

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/6 
The second stage focuses on the same functionality developed, but drawing from a transaction hash. To achieve this, we integrated an indexer, which, in our case, was Blockfrost, after a quick research into different possible options. Either way, everything is more or less modular to a later integration of other indexers.
 https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/7 
・With Blockfrost integration, we implemented the functionality to display the transaction diagram based on the transaction hash.

 https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/10

ms.promise:
Definition of a DSL capable of specifying a Cardano transaction. 
Documentation describing precisely the language and boilerplate of the implementation of a parser.
ms.criteria: The user or Cardano developer is able to write sentences in the defined Domain Specific Language that specify Cardano transactions.
ms.report:
DSL capable of specifying a Cardano transaction. 
We have created the documentation precisely describing the language to specify Cardano transactions that can later be used to generate a compliance CBOR and implemented the language data types. The previously mentioned documentation can be found in the repository:
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/blob/main/docs/specification.md 
Key achievements:
・Definition of DSL
・JSON Schema
・Examples of transactions written in the DSL
・Prototype of parser using the JSON Schema
・PoC interface to try the prototype

To define the DSL, an iteration was performed over a simple example: transferring ADA from one wallet to another. In this way, the most important sections of the transaction were defined: the definition of inputs and outputs.
The example was then iterated upon to expand the language's expressiveness, defining how to describe inputs and outputs. Other sections were also identified, such as fees, minting, withdrawals, and even sections that are irrelevant or imperceptible in a CBOR, like names (for inputs, outputs, or the transaction itself), among others.
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/68 https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/69
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/73
After the specification was done, we defined a JSON Schema to aid the checking the syntaxis of transactions written on the DSL.
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/71
A video-demo was recorded showing the main uses of the DSL.
Video

ms.promise: Implementation of a parser/code-generator for reading a tx spec written in the DSL and producing a CBOR.
ms.criteria: A sentence in the DSL can be parsed and a CBOR is generated.
ms.report:
1- A parser for reading a tx spec written in the DSL and producing a CBOR. 

We have developed and implemented a parser and translation function for transactions written in the domain-specific language (DSL). This functionality enables the generation of CBOR representations, which can be displayed in either hexadecimal or diagnostic notation, providing flexibility for further analysis.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/77
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/79
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/80

In the previous milestone we defined the DSL, with which we can now build transactions and parse them in a simple way. Then, the result of these transactions can be displayed using the previously developed grapher. The web application was adjusted to facilitate this type of operations.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/85
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/84

We also identify cases that can't be directly written as CBOR and implement appropriate case management. These cases were also properly documented.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/78
https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/81

Once the implementation was completed, tests were performed on the functions that parse the CBOR to ensure its correct working.

https://github.com/txpipe-shop/cardano-graphical-tx/issues/82

2-A video-demo was recorded showing the main uses of the DSL.

https://youtu.be/5-c2tF_etSE
